headline: Lancashire's Tree-Planting Volunteers Plant Half a Million Trees
meta_description: Nearly 500,000 trees planted across Lancashire in two seasons create new woodlands, orchards, and wildlife habitats.
summary_short: Volunteers across Lancashire have planted almost 500,000 trees over two planting seasons, establishing new woodlands and orchards.
body:
Almost 500,000 trees have been planted across Lancashire, UK by volunteers working across two planting seasons. The effort has created new woodlands, orchards, and habitats for wildlife across the region.

This sustained commitment reflects a growing recognition of trees' role in addressing environmental challenges while building community connection to the land. The mix of woodland and orchard plantings suggests a thoughtful approach—combining ecological restoration with productive landscapes that support both nature and people.

The scale of the achievement—nearly half a million trees in just two seasons—demonstrates what coordinated volunteer action can accomplish when people unite around a shared vision for their region's future.

Two planting seasons completed by volunteers
New woodlands, orchards, and wildlife habitats created
